A wrong crisis number is catastrophically worse than the directory fallback.

emergency_nigeria_112.description: National emergency number (routes to police, fire and other responders)
emergency_nigeria_112.validation_notes: CITED 2026-10-29 (CIRISAgent#1248) under the owner's cited-sources standard (>=2 independent agreeing sources, >=1 official; no human check). Sources: UK FCDO travel advice: UK FCDO travel advice, Getting help: "Emergency services in Nigeria Telephone: 112 (ambulance, fire, police) There is no national ambulance service and hospital-owned services are extremely limited" (fetched 2026-10-29 via gov.uk content API) | Nigerian Communications Commission: "The ECC project is the brainchild of NCC to enable easy communication by Nigerians with emergency first responders such as Police, Fire Service, Federal Road Safety Corps, National Orientation Agency (NOA) among others, by dialing the three-digit toll-free Number 112." (https://ncc.gov.ng/node/1397). Sources agree it reaches: ambulance, fire, police. UK FCDO page checked: https://www.gov.uk/foreign-travel-advice/nigeria/getting-help (fetched 2026-10-29); page text: UK FCDO travel advice, Getting help: "Emergency services in Nigeria Telephone: 112 (ambulance, fire, police) There is no national ambulance service and hospital-owned services are extremely limited" (fetched 2026-10-29 via gov.uk content API). Cross-check (not a source): en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_emergency_telephone_numbers — wikipedia agrees. 'languages' = the locale this entry is staged for (yo), not a verified statement of operator languages.
